Title: Reliquiae sacrae, sive Auctorum fere jam perditorum secundi tertiique saeculi post Christum natum quae supersunt; accedunt Synodi, et Epistolae canonicae, Nicaeno concilio antiquiores. Editio altera, Vol. I
Creator: Martin Joseph Routh (editor); fragments of Quadratus, Aristides, Aristo of Pella, Melito of Sardis, Claudius Apollinaris, Dionysius of Corinth, Hegesippus and others, with Routh's Latin notes
Publisher: Oxford: e typographeo academico, 1846 (title page MDCCCXLVI), editio altera
Publication Date: 1846
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication); the item record carries no rights field
Language: lat (mixed: Routh's Latin introductions and notes with the Greek fragments and Latin versions; the Greek is a minority of the letters)
Source: Internet Archive item reliquiaesacraes01rout, full-text OCR file reliquiaesacraes01rout_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Claude), 2026-09-29. The item record gives no possible-copyright-status or licence; contributor Robarts - University of Toronto (item reliquiaesacraes01rout, one of a set reliquiaesacraes01-05rout). Title page read in the OCR: 'RELIQUIAE SACRAE, SIVE, AUCTORUM FERE JAM PERDITORUM SECUNDI TERTIIQUE SAECULI POST CHRISTUM NATUM QUAE SUPERSUNT ... AD CODICES MSS. RECENSUIT, NOTISQUE ILLUSTRAVIT, MARTINUS JOSEPHUS ROUTH ... EDITIO ALTERA. VOL. I. OXONII: E TYPOGRAPHEO ACADEMICO. MDCCCXLVI'. Vol. V (reliquiaesacraes05rout, 1848) was checked and holds Archelaus, Rebaptismate and creeds, not the apologists; it is not vendored.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged, apart from this header. Rights basis: the 1846 title-page date clears this registry's public-domain-by-date rule; the host record is silent. OCR artifacts, running heads, line numbers and apparatus left as found; nothing was corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Measured on the OCR before vendoring: 129464 Greek-script characters.
Content note: Vol. I holds, among others: Quadratus and Aristides (the Quadratus fragment and the Aristides testimonia and notes), Aristo of Pella, Melito of Sardis (fragments and index of works), Claudius Apollinaris, Dionysius of Corinth, Hegesippus. Routh's Greek runs in parallel columns with Latin, and the OCR interleaves the columns line by line; the Greek layer is present (about 129,000 Greek-script characters) but has accent and letter errors and mixed-column line breaks; the front matter is scan noise. SECOND WITNESS: check every Greek reading against the page image. Miltiades is not in this volume.
